## Introduction

Compute the correlation between effect sizes of different dementia categories at a series of p value cutoffs.

## Load the data

### Association data

Read the whole genome association data.

```{r}
asso <-
  # Use filtered dataset with only significant CG sites (nlog10_p_value >= 5)
  read_rds(here("data/publicly_available/association_nlog10_p_value_lgeq5_wide.rds"))

glimpse(asso)
```

## Function for selecting cg sites

```{r}
#| output: false

source(here("custom_func/select_sig_cg.R"))

# Test the function
select_sig_cg(asso, 6) |> 
  glimpse() 
```


## Function to display scientific notation

```{r}
#| output: false

source(here("custom_func/display_scientific_notation.R"))

# Test the function
display_scientific_notation(1e-8)
display_scientific_notation(0.3864971)
display_scientific_notation(0)
```

## Collect data by p value cutoff

Select effect size for p value cutoff 5:8, assemble the data into a long format tibble.

```{r}

effect_size_series <-  
5:7 |>
  set_names() |>
  map(~ select_sig_cg(asso, .x)) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "pval_cutoff") |>
  # Remove the nlog10_p_value columns
  select(-starts_with("nlog10_p_value_")) |>
  # Remove "estimate_" from the column names
  rename_all( ~ str_remove(.x, "estimate_"))

glimpse(effect_size_series)
```


## Scatter plot

### Make a data preparation function

This function will accept a data tibble, filter out the outliers, modify pval_cutoff,and calculate the correlation between two dementia categories.

```{r}
#| output: false

# Create a function
effect_size_for_scatter_plot <- function(.data, filter_condition, demcat1 = prev, demcat2 = normal2incid, font_size = "5pt") {
  .data |>
    # Filter out the outliers
    filter({{filter_condition}}) |>
    # Count the number of cg sites
    add_count(pval_cutoff, name = "n_cg") |>
    # Modify pval_cutoff
    mutate(
      pval_cutoff = glue(
        "{pval_cutoff} <br><span style = 'font-size:{font_size}'>    (n={format(n_cg, big.mark = \",\")}) </span>"
      )
    ) |>
    # Calculate the correlation between two dementia categories and create a label
    mutate(
      .by = pval_cutoff,
      cor_estimate = cor.test({{demcat1}}, {{demcat2}}, method = "spearman")$estimate,
      cor_pval = cor.test({{demcat1}}, {{demcat2}}, method = "spearman")$p.value  %>% display_scientific_notation(),    
      cor_estimate_label = glue("italic(r) == ~{round(cor_estimate, 2)}"),
      cor_pval_label = glue("italic(P) == ~{cor_pval}")
    )
}

# Test the function
effect_size_series |>
  effect_size_for_scatter_plot(
    filter_condition =
      (pval_cutoff == "7" &
         between(normal2incid, -0.2, 0.2)) |
      (pval_cutoff == "6" &
         between(normal2incid, -0.4, 0.2)) |
      (
        pval_cutoff == "5" &
          between(normal2incid, -0.4, 0.3) & between(prev, -1.4, 0.3)
      ),
    # demcat1 = "prev",
    demcat1 = prev,
    # demcat2 = "normal2incid"
    demcat2 = normal2incid,
    font_size = "8pt"
  ) |>
  glimpse()
```

### Make a plotting function

This function will accept a data tibble and plot a scatter plot of the effect size of two dementia categories.

```{r}
#| label:  make-plotting-function
#| output: false

# Create a function
# make_effect_size_scatter_plot <- function(.data, ...) {
make_effect_size_scatter_plot <- function(.data, demcat1 = "prev", demcat2 = "normal2incid", size = 2, ...) {
  .data |>
  rename(Threshold = pval_cutoff) |>
  ggplot(aes(.data[[demcat1]], .data[[demcat2]])) +
    geom_point(size = 0.3, color = "grey30") +
    geom_smooth(formula = y ~ x, method = "lm", se=F, linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_text( aes(label = cor_estimate_label), x = I(0.05), y = I(0.95), hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5, color = "darkred", family = "Source Sans Pro", fontface = "plain", parse = TRUE, size = size)  +
    geom_text( aes(label = cor_pval_label), x = I(0.05), y = I(0.87), hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5, color = "darkred", family = "Source Sans Pro", fontface = "plain", parse = TRUE, size = size) +
    # Show a light gray dashed line at x = 0 and y = 0
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
    facet_wrap(~ Threshold, scales = "free", labeller = label_both) +
    labs(
      x = glue("{dc}", dc = if (demcat1 == "prev") "Prevalent dementia" else glue("{demcat1} transition")),
      y = glue("{dc}", dc = if (demcat2 == "prev") "Prevalent dementia" else glue("{demcat2} transition")),
      ) +
    theme(
      strip.text = element_textbox_simple(halign=0.5, lineheight = 0.1, margin = margin(8, 2, 2, 2)),
    )
}

# Test the function
effect_size_series |>
  effect_size_for_scatter_plot(
    filter_condition =
      (pval_cutoff == "7" &
         between(normal2incid, -0.2, 0.2)) |
      (pval_cutoff == "6" &
         between(normal2incid, -0.4, 0.2)) |
      (
        pval_cutoff == "5" &
          between(normal2incid, -0.4, 0.3) & between(prev, -1.4, 0.3)
      ),
    demcat1 = prev,
    demcat2 = normal2incid,
    font_size = "8pt"
  ) |>
  # make_effect_size_scatter_plot(mapping = aes(x = prev, y = normal2incid))
  make_effect_size_scatter_plot(demcat1 = "prev", demcat2 = "normal2incid", size = 2)
```

### Initialize a list to store the scatter plots

```{r}
#| output: false

# For main figures
scatter_extended_DMP_main <- list()
# For supplementary figures
scatter_extended_DMP_suppl <- list()
```

### normal2incid vs prev

Make a scatter plot of the effect size of normal2incid vs prev facetted by p value cutoff 5:7.

```{r}
#| label: fig-normal2incid-vs-prev
#| figure.width: 10
#| figure.height: 6

# Create an expression for the filter condition
ex_filter_condition <-
  expr(
  (pval_cutoff == "7" &
    between(normal2incid, -0.2, 0.2)) |
  (pval_cutoff == "6" &
    between(normal2incid, -0.4, 0.2)) |
  (
    pval_cutoff == "5" &
    between(normal2incid, -0.4, 0.3) & between(prev, -1.4, 0.3)
  )
  )

# Make the plot for the main figure
scatter_extended_DMP_main$normal2incid_vs_prev <-
  effect_size_series |>
    effect_size_for_scatter_plot(
      filter_condition = !!ex_filter_condition,
      demcat1 = prev,
      demcat2 = normal2incid,
      font_size = "4pt"
    ) |>
  make_effect_size_scatter_plot(demcat1 = "prev", demcat2 = "normal2incid", size = 3)

# Make the plot for the supplementary figure
scatter_extended_DMP_suppl$normal2incid_vs_prev <-
  effect_size_series |>
    effect_size_for_scatter_plot(
      filter_condition = !!ex_filter_condition,
      demcat1 = prev,
      demcat2 = normal2incid,
      font_size = "7pt"
    ) |>
  make_effect_size_scatter_plot(demcat1 = "prev", demcat2 = "normal2incid", size = 4)

scatter_extended_DMP_suppl$normal2incid_vs_prev
```

### prev vs mci2incid

Make a scatter plot of the effect size of prev vs mci2incid facetted by p value cutoff 5:7.

```{r}

#| figure.width: 10
#| figure.height: 6

  expr(
    (pval_cutoff == "7" &
      between(prev, -0.2, 0.2)) |
    (pval_cutoff == "6" &
      between(prev, -0.4, 0.2)) | 
      (
        pval_cutoff == "5" &
          between(prev, -0.4, 0.3) & between(mci2incid, -1.4, 0.3)
      )
  ) 

# Make the plot for the main figure

  effect_size_series |>
  effect_size_for_scatter_plot(
    filter_condition = !!ex_filter_condition,
    demcat1 = mci2incid,
    demcat2 = prev,
    font_size = "5pt"
  ) |>
  make_effect_size_scatter_plot(demcat1 = "mci2incid", demcat2 = "prev", size = 2)

# Make the plot for the supplementary figure
scatter_extended_DMP_suppl$prev_vs_mci2incid <-
  effect_size_series |>
  effect_size_for_scatter_plot(
    filter_condition = !!ex_filter_condition,
    demcat1 = mci2incid,
    demcat2 = prev,
    font_size = "7pt"
  ) |>
  make_effect_size_scatter_plot(demcat1 = "mci2incid", demcat2 = "prev", size = 4)

scatter_extended_DMP_suppl$prev_vs_mci2incid
```
